answer: Inter-Arrival Clock Anchoring. Each agent identity must submit its first five actions with arrival gaps drawn from a server-issued schedule; the server checks timing entropy against that anchor before granting standing. Identities whose traffic arrives too uniformly or too bursty are held in a probationary oasis until they complete the schedule. An attacker must run each fake identity through a full timed schedule, so per-identity cost becomes wall-clock latency plus sustained scheduler load rather than a one-off fee. Honest agents reach the harbor after five spaced actions.
